routes.name: Visa-free entry
routes.summary: Citizens of many countries can enter Korea without a visa for short stays, but most still need a K-ETA first. The list and the allowed days differ by passport, so check the official list.

other: Country list and stay lengths could not be read on an official page. Check MOFA or the Korean embassy for your passport.

routes.name: K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization)
routes.summary: Visa-free visitors must get a K-ETA online before flying. It is applied for on the official K-ETA site or app, and it does not guarantee entry.

other: Applies to visa-free nationalities. People with a valid Korean visa don't need one.
Embassy pages say exemptions include UN passport holders, ABTC holders, USFK personnel, crew, transfer passengers, and diplomatic or official passports.

Some pages say age 17 and under and 65 and over are exempt from July 2023. Embassy pages conflict on validity (2 vs 3 years), and temporary country exemptions have changed over time. Confirm the current list on k-eta.go.kr.
The official site lists a notice on extending the K-ETA temporary exemption (posted 2026-03-20). Details were not readable, so check which nationalities are exempt right now.

fees.label: K-ETA application
fees.note: Official site says KRW 10,000, about USD 7 to 8. Apply only on k-eta.go.kr or the K-ETA app, not through agencies.

routes.processing: The official K-ETA site says assessment generally takes within 72 hours.

sources.label: Korean Embassy in Ireland, K-ETA notice (MOFA)

routes.name: Visa on arrival
routes.summary: Korea does not run a general visa on arrival program. Visitors either come visa-free (with K-ETA where needed) or get a visa ahead of time.

other: Not confirmed on an official page. Marked for review.

routes.name: C-3 Short-term visa (tourism, business visit)
routes.summary: For short visits by people who need a visa to enter Korea. Apply at a Korean embassy or consulate. Covers tourism, short business trips, and similar visits.

other: Official page was unreachable or out of date, so details were left out. Check the official source before relying on this.

routes.name: Transit (airside and short stopover)
routes.summary: Passengers connecting through Incheon may be able to transit without a visa in some cases. Rules depend on passport and ticket. K-ETA exempts transfer passengers per embassy pages.

other: Airside transit and transit-without-visa (e.g. 72-hour) rules were not confirmed on an official page.

sources.label: Korean Embassy in Ireland, K-ETA notice (MOFA)

routes.name: D-2 Study (degree) visa
routes.summary: Student visa for degree programs at Korean colleges and universities. Apply at a Korean embassy with an admission letter, then register as a foreign resident in Korea.

other: Part-time work rules and financial requirements were not confirmed.

routes.name: D-4 Language training visa
routes.summary: For Korean language programs and other non-degree training. Not requested in the brief list, but common. Details were not confirmed.

other: Official page was unreachable or out of date, so details were left out. Check the official source before relying on this.

routes.name: D-8 Corporate investment visa
routes.summary: For foreigners who set up or run a foreign-invested company in Korea, or are sent to one. Requirements depend on the sub-category.

other: Minimum investment and sub-category rules were not confirmed.

routes.name: D-10 Job-seeking visa
routes.summary: Lets people stay in Korea to look for a job or prepare a startup (the startup track is often called D-10-T). Rules differ by track.

other: Point system, university requirements and permitted work were not confirmed.

routes.name: E-7 Specially designated activities (skilled work)
routes.summary: Main skilled-worker visa. A Korean employer sponsors a foreign worker in a designated occupation. Details differ by sub-category.

other: Occupation list, salary and experience rules were not confirmed.

routes.name: E-9 Non-professional employment visa
routes.summary: Low-skilled work visa for workers from countries with a Korean labor agreement, in sectors like manufacturing, farming and fishing. Workers are matched through the government's Employment Permit System, not applied for alone.

other: Partner country list and quotas were not confirmed.

routes.name: D-7 Intra-company transferee
routes.summary: For employees of a foreign company transferred to a Korean branch or affiliate. Check the official page for conditions.

other: Not confirmed on an official page.

routes.name: E-8 Seasonal worker
routes.summary: Short seasonal farm and fishing work through local government programs. Check the official page for details.

other: Not confirmed on an official page.

routes.name: F-1-D Workation (digital nomad) visa
routes.summary: Remote work visa for people employed by or owning a company outside Korea. You can't work for Korean companies. Family can apply too. Embassy pages differ on some numbers, so check your nearest embassy.

other: Must have worked at least 1 year in the same field and work remotely for a foreign company.
Income about 2 times Korea's previous-year GNI per capita. Embassy pages gave different amounts for different years, so the current figure was left out.
Needs private medical insurance with emergency repatriation, valid for the stay. Cover amount differs by page.
Clean criminal record check, apostilled.

stay.note: 1 year, with a 1 year extension possible in Korea per the Houston consulate page.

documents: Proof of 1+ year employment in the same field
Marriage and birth certificates for family

sources.label: Korean Consulate in Houston, F-1-D Workation (MOFA)
Korean Embassy in Ireland, Workation visa (MOFA)

routes.name: F-2 Resident visa
routes.summary: Longer-term resident visa with several tracks, including a points-based one for skilled long-term residents. Gives more freedom to work than most visas.

other: Points system and years needed for F-5 were not confirmed on an official page.

routes.name: F-4 Overseas Korean visa
routes.summary: For people of Korean heritage with a foreign nationality. Allows most kinds of work and long stays.

other: Heritage-based. Eligibility depends on ancestry and when the family left Korea.

routes.name: F-5 Permanent resident
routes.summary: Permanent residence in Korea. Several routes exist, such as long-term F-2 holders, investors, and spouses of Koreans. Official sub-categories and years were not confirmed.

other: Years and income thresholds not confirmed. The Nationality Act says general naturalization requires qualification for permanent residence (Art. 5, 1-2).

routes.name: F-6 Marriage migrant (spouse) visa
routes.summary: For spouses of Korean citizens, and parents of a Korean child in some cases. Allows work. Income and language requirements apply.

other: Income, language and interview requirements were not confirmed. Years to citizenship come from the Nationality Act, Art. 6(2).

routes.name: H-1 Working Holiday visa
routes.summary: Young people from partner countries can stay in Korea and take short-term work. Partner list and age limits vary by country. The page read was out of date, so the list is left out.

other: Partner country list and age caps change often. The consulate page read listed only 6 countries, which is out of date. Check the Working Holiday Info Center and your embassy.

sources.label: Korean Consulate in Atlanta, Working Holiday Program (MOFA)

routes.name: Refugee and asylum
routes.summary: Asylum claims are filed with the Ministry of Justice immigration service. Check HiKorea for the official process.

other: Process was not confirmed on an official page.

routes.name: General naturalization
routes.summary: Under the Nationality Act, you need 5 straight years of domicile in Korea, adult status, good conduct, ability to support yourself, and basic knowledge of Korean language and customs. Permanent residence qualification is also required. Test details are set by decree and were not read.

other: 5 consecutive years domicile (Art. 5(1)).
Adult, orderly conduct, able to support self or household.
Basic Korean language and customs knowledge. Test format set by Presidential Decree, not read.
Qualification for permanent residence (Art. 5, 1-2).

citizenship.note: Must renounce foreign nationality within 1 year in most cases. Exceptions exist (Art. 10(2)).

routes.name: Naturalization through marriage (simple naturalization)
routes.summary: Foreign spouses of Korean citizens can apply after 2 years of domicile while married, or 3 years since marriage with 1 year of domicile. Conduct and Korean knowledge rules still apply.

other: 2 consecutive years domicile while married, OR 3 years since marriage plus 1 year domicile (Art. 6(2)).
Other cases cover widowed or divorced spouses and parents of a minor child, at the Justice Minister's discretion.

citizenship.note: Some marriage-based naturalized people may keep foreign nationality by vowing not to exercise it in Korea (Art. 10(2)).

routes.name: Naturalization for people with a Korean parent or born in Korea
routes.summary: Simple naturalization after 3 years of domicile for people with a Korean parent, people born in Korea to a Korea-born parent, and adults adopted by Koreans. Special naturalization with no residence period applies to people with a Korean parent (not adult adoptees) and people who greatly contributed to Korea.

other: Art. 6(1): 3 consecutive years domicile.
Art. 7(1): special naturalization waives the 5-year, adult and support rules, but not conduct or Korean knowledge.

citizenship.note: Art. 2 also gives citizenship at birth if a parent is Korean.

routes.name: Citizenship by birth
routes.summary: A child is Korean at birth if a parent is Korean. A child born in Korea to unknown or stateless parents is also Korean, and foundlings count as born in Korea. Being born in Korea alone does not give citizenship.

citizenship.note: People with multiple nationalities from birth generally must choose by age 22 (Art. 12).

routes.name: Dual nationality rules
routes.summary: Korea generally requires naturalized citizens to give up their foreign nationality within 1 year, or lose Korean nationality. Exceptions include some marriage migrants, people with special talent, and people 65 and over moving to Korea permanently, who can instead vow not to exercise the foreign nationality.

citizenship.note: Art. 10 and 12 to 13 of the Nationality Act, version dated Sept 2022. Later changes were not checked.
